errors.evidence: The plot does not have a title. "The exploration of hyperparameters" is the caption from the source paper, not a title on the figure itself.

errors.text_span: a variable labeled "N" on the x-axis
errors.evidence: The x-axis is labeled with the Greek letter alpha (α), not "N".
The labeled tick marks on the x-axis range from 0 to 4, but the data extends to an x-value of 5, which is beyond the last tick mark.
The description omits the units for the y-axis, which are given as a percentage (%) in the label "Accuracy (%)".
The data point at x=0 has a y-value that is visibly below the 22.75 gridline, closer to 22.70.

errors.text_span: at N=1, Performance peaks at approximately 23.75;
errors.evidence: The peak performance of 23.75 occurs at an x-value of approximately 0.5, not at x=1. At x=1, the accuracy value is approximately 23.4.

errors.text_span: at N=2, Performance drops to approximately 23.25;
errors.evidence: There is no data point at x=2. The description invents this data point.

errors.text_span: and at N=4, Performance further declines to approximately 22.75.
errors.evidence: There is no data point at x=4. The final data point is at x=5, with a value slightly below 22.75.

errors.text_span: a steady, linear decrease across the remaining range of N
errors.evidence: The decrease after the peak consists of two line segments with visibly different slopes (from x≈0.5 to x=1, and from x=1 to x=5), so describing it as a single 'steady, linear decrease' is inaccurate.
